children: , the world's largest contract chipmaker, slipped roughly 0.4% to $416.60 Tuesday as MediaTek rolled out the first Dimensity processor built on TSMC's cutting-edge 2-nanometer process. The Dimensity 9600 Pro is aimed squarely at premium smartphones from Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo, giving TSMC's newest manufacturing node an early showcase in one of the world's biggest consumer-chip markets.

MediaTek's announcement says the new processor delivers 51% higher large-language-model prefill performance, 55% more token generation per watt and 61% lower multicore power consumption versus its predecessor. Smartphones powered by the chip are expected to arrive this quarter. Those are MediaTek's own test results, so real-world devices will ultimately determine how much of that performance survives outside the lab. Still, the launch puts TSMC's 2-nanometer technology directly into the AI-on-device race rather than leaving it as a manufacturing roadmap story.

The valuation picture adds a note of caution. At $416.60, TSMC trades 14.65% above its GuruFocus GF Value of $363.38, suggesting investors are already paying a meaningful premium for future growth. TSMC generated $40.2 billion of second-quarter revenue with a 67.7% gross margin, while 2-nanometer products represented only 3% of wafer revenue. MediaTek gives the technology an important commercial proof point, but the bigger question is scale: yields, wafer pricing and customer volume will determine whether 2-nanometer moves from an impressive technical milestone into TSMC's next major earnings engine.

title: TSMC Slips as 2-Nanometer Chip Powers a 51% AI Leap
